summary: Run 11 defines a low-access, owner-reviewed brief for one approved offer and two named channels but defers a SKILL.md search. A distinct output does not by itself establish a distinct skill-selection job.

Practitioner discussions describe one-page and template-based briefs; Asana describes a connected campaign workflow. These sources do not measure unmet need, relative performance, time saved or marketing outcomes.

The proposed brief would separate approved facts from drafts and unknowns, check caps, consent, destinations and measurements, and stop before account or spend action. These are hypothetical validation rules, not a tested package capability.
The next research question is prelaunch QA and UTM/naming governance from an approved brief, compared with a spreadsheet checklist or connected platform QA. No seventh card was added.

No campaign-planning package was sought, opened, installed or run. The defined first-use workflow is a specification, not a validated skill or marketing result.
